entries.narrative:
When you came into the world there was a profound peace that came over the delivery room. It stayed there, as we met you, and held you for the first time. It was as if divinity itself had decended.

In that moment I learned that the true nature of existence was that everything is okay, it was not scary like I thought until then. I wondered if the nurses and doctors were aware of it! It was like a miracle, bello.

That was the most beautiful moment of my life. That is your incredible spirit.

"Alfred and dad!" That was something I always used to say to you. "Alfred and dad!" I would say. "Best friends!"

You're still my best friend. And you always will be.

entries.narrative:
When you were young my bello you looked so weird! We thought maybe you would be weird looking when you grew up, and I would say "I will love him anyway he looks". I would say, "He is going to be such a great person it won't matter!". 

I wish I could go home, more than anything, to hug you every day.
entries.title: Mummy's blue pyjamas

entries.narrative:
On the night before you were born, there were two omens, and there was one omen when you were born: three in total.

First, there was a wolf that we saw. Okay, it was a husky. Still, it was a sign.

Next, I found a two dollar coin on the street. The highest possible coin, the highest possible luck.

Finally, one of the midwives was called Asha. Asha means highest truth, bello. Just like your name: Verissimo.

entries.narrative: This was my worst nightmare. And it happened. You look like you have been crying for hours for someone to make it all better, and you don't know what else to do. I'm sorry this was done to you, my bello. I never would have allowed it to happen, and I did everything in my power to stop it, even getting sent to prison. You will be there again tomorrow, and I don't know what to do about it. My life is hell knowing that you suffer weekly. One day, daddy will return.

I tried to see you for these past two months, but your mother said I could not. She has kept us apart.

My beloved Alfred
entries.narrative:
Dear Alfred,

It's been over two weeks since I last saw you. I love you very, very much, and I miss you more than words can say.

I can only imagine how much your dad misses you, so much more than me.

I am so sorry you came into this world with so much disagreement between your parents. I do think your mum and your dad love you very much, but it seems they disagree on some things.

I know for sure your dad loves you so much, and he is doing the best he can to see you as soon as possible. Unfortunately, your mum is not understanding how your dad would give up anything just to spend time with you. He loves you more than his life, and understandably so. He is willing to give your mum everything, just to be with you.

I don't know why your mum is not understanding the love your dad has for you.

Alfred, you are the most beautiful and amazing baby in the world. I had the pleasure of looking after you for a few days last month. Unfortunately, your mother blocked me for some reason, so I cannot ask her if I can come over to see you, play with you and love you so much.

For some reason, I don't know why, she will not allow your dad or me anywhere near you.

If my heart is broken, imagine how much more broken your dad's heart must be.

Alfred, you will not be six months old forever. One day, you will ask questions and want to know why your dad and your Nonna have not been there, why we have been missing you, and why we have missed out on this precious time with you — time your dad and I will never get back.

Yes, it's true, your parents had disagreements, but which parents don't? Your Nonno and I had arguments, but I never called the police or had an AVO against him.

Your mother destroyed your dad's life, and she knows it. Maybe it was her plan to marry and have a child so that she could get her Australian citizenship.

I can tell you that I loved your mother better than a daughter. She lived with me while she was pregnant with you, and I waited on her and looked after all her needs.

I really would have liked her to have a discussion with me about what she thinks I did that was so bad, in her eyes, to merit her blocking me, so that I could not have any contact with her or you, my beloved Alfred.

All I can say is, you reap what you sow. I thought your mother loved God, but it is what it is. She has done, and is doing, what she wants to do.

Alfred, I do pray for you, for your mother and for your dad. I pray that you will grow up knowing and loving God.

You are a beautiful baby, and God loves you.

I am so proud to be your grandmother, even though I can't see you. You look so much like your dad — identical to your dad! I see him in you every day when I look at the photos and videos I have taken.

I want to see you soon, my beloved, to see how you smile and laugh, to play with you and to read books to you.

Your dad wrote you a book, and he's going to write you another one. He just loves you so much.

So here's to hoping and praying that we will all be together very soon, very soon, my love.

Don't worry. We will make up for the lost time, I'm sure.

I love you with all my heart.

Bye, gorgeous. Bye.
